articles.title: Cyclist dead after being struck, trapped under school bus in downtown Toronto
articles.summary: A man has died after being hit by a bus and getting trapped underneath it in downtown Toronto early Wednesday, first responders say.

articles.summary: A man has died after being struck by a school bus in downtown Toronto on Wednesday morning. articles.title: Joly ‘convinced’ Ottawa can find a path forward with Stellantis as talks continue
articles.summary: TORONTO — Industry Minister Mélanie Joly says she's "convinced" the federal government and Stellantis can find a path forward amid fallout from the automaker's deal to sell its Brampton, Ont., assembly plant to defence contractor Roshel.

articles.title: Port Credit’s waterfront mega-development reaches new milestone
articles.summary: Construction on a new neighbourhood in Mississauga’s waterfront — decades in the making — is about a third done, with no completion date set yet. CBC’s Jayden Dill breaks down the transformation of the land, and the developer's plans for the future.

articles.title: Stellantis taking Unifor to court over alleged obstruction of environmental assessment
articles.summary: The ongoing dispute over the sale of Stellantis's Brampton, Ont., assembly plant is heading to court, as the automaker has filed a lawsuit alleging Unifor is impeding an environmental assessment necessary to the transaction.

articles.title: Constable who shot Jamal Francique says he acted out of 'fight-or-flight' instinct
articles.summary: A police officer who shot a Black man in the head during an attempted arrest in Mississauga, Ont., nearly seven years ago offered condolences to the man's grieving family Tuesday as he began testifying at a coroner's inquest.

articles.title: Anthem singer apologizes for botched O Canada lyrics at Leafs game against Islanders
articles.summary: The anthem singer at the Toronto Maple Leafs game against New York Monday night apologized on social media after singing the wrong lyrics to the Canadian national anthem.

articles.title: Spike in emissions a major setback in GTA climate goals: report
articles.summary: A more polluting energy grid and rising demand for gas heating during a colder winter drove the largest annual spike in planet-warming emissions in at least a decade across the Greater Toronto and Hamilton Area, a new report found, putting the region further off track of its climate goals.
